The statement below is the form most directly useful in what follows.\\n   111\\t\\n   112\\t% The paper states this result in a theorem environment with the label lem:ld-soundness.\\n   113\\t% We keep both the environment and the label verbatim for cross-reference fidelity.\\n   114\\t\\\\begin{theorem}[Quantum soundness of the simultaneous classical low individual degree test]\\\\label{lem:ld-soundness}\\n   115\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:ld-game, def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:projective-strategy-general, def:tensor-product-value, def:povm-distance, def:bracket}\\n   116\\t\\tThere exists a function\\n   117\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   118\\t\\t\\t\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps, q, m, d, k) = a\\\\,(dmk)^a \\\\bigl(\\\\eps^b + q^{-b} + 2^{-bmd}\\\\bigr)\\n   119\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   120\\t\\tfor universal constants $a \\\\ge 1$ and $0 < b \\\\le 1$ such that the following holds. For all $\\\\eps > 0$ and every parameter tuple $\\\\mathsf{ldparams} = (q,m,d,k)$ as in Definition~\\\\ref{def:ld-game} (so $q$ is an admissible field size and $m$ divides $q$), and for all projective strategies $(\\\\psi, A, B)$ that succeed with probability at least $1-\\\\eps$ in the game $\\\\mathcal G^{\\\\mathrm{ld}}_{\\\\mathsf{ldparams}}$, there exist measurements\\n   121\\t\\t\\\\[\\n   122\\t\\t\\tG^w \\\\in \\\\mathrm{PolyMeas}(m,q,d,k)\\n   123\\t\\t\\\\]\\n   124\\t\\ton $\\\\hilb_w$ for $w \\\\in \\\\{\\\\mathrm A,\\\\mathrm B\\\\}$, where by slight abuse of notation $m$, $q$, $d$ denote the constant tuples $(m,\\\\ldots,m)$, $(q,\\\\ldots,q)$, $(d,\\\\ldots,d)$ of length $k$, such that\\n   125\\t\\t\\\\begin{align*}\\n   126\\t\\t\\tA^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   127\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   128\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   129\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{[(g_1(u),\\\\ldots,g_k(u)) = (a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k)]} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   130\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   131\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot B^{\\\\mathsf{Point},\\\\, u}_{a_1,\\\\ldots,a_k}\\\\;,\\\\\\\\\\n   132\\t\\t\\tG^{\\\\mathrm A}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k} \\\\ot I_{\\\\mathrm B}\\n   133\\t\\t\\t&\\\\approx_{\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}}\\n   134\\t\\t\\tI_{\\\\mathrm A} \\\\ot G^{\\\\mathrm B}_{g_1,\\\\ldots,g_k}\\\\;,\\n   135\\t\\t\\\\end{align*}\\n   136\\t\\twhere $\\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}} = \\\\delta_{\\\\mathrm{ld}}(\\\\eps,q,m,d,k)$, all three approximations are with respect to the state $\\\\ket{\\\\psi}$, and the bracket notation for post-processed outcomes is that of Definition~\\\\ref{def:bracket}. The first two approximations hold on average over the uniform distribution on $u \\\\in \\\\F_q^m$; no question distribution is associated with the third.\\n   137\\t\\\\end{theorem}\\n   138\\t\\\\begin{proof}\\n   139\\t\\t\\\\uses{def:ld-question-distribution, def:ld-win-predicate, def:ld-meas, def:povm-distance}\\n   140\\t\\tLet $\\\\Sigma = \\\\F_q$ and let $\\\\code \\\\subseteq \\\\Sigma^q$ be the Reed--Solomon code of degree $d$: the set of all $(p(x_1),\\\\ldots,p(x_q))$ where $p\\\\colon \\\\F_q \\\\to \\\\F_q$ is a univariate polynomial of degree at most $d$ and $x_1,\\\\ldots,x_q$ enumerate $\\\\F_q$. 1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
     2	# github-sync.sh — push this repository to its GitHub home,
     3	# git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git (standalone repo since the
     4	# 2026-08-31 restructure; the old subtree-into-monorepo flow is retired,
     5	# see EVOLUTION.md). Run after every merge to main.
     6	set -euo pipefail
     7	ROOT="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/../.." && pwd)"
     8	_common="$(git -C "$ROOT" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null || true)"
     9	case "$_common" in */.git) ROOT="$(dirname "$_common")" ;; esac
    10	cd "$ROOT"
    11	git remote get-url github >/dev/null 2>&1 || git remote add github git@github.com:Dengnifer/MIPStarRE-A.git
    12	for i in 1 2 3 4 5; do
    13	  git push github --all && { echo "github-sync: pushed $(git rev-parse --short main)"; exit 0; }
    14	  echo "github-sync: push attempt $i failed; retrying" >&2; sleep 15
    15	done
    16	echo "github-sync: all push attempts failed" >&2; exit 1

    57	GENERATED_HEADINGS = (

    61	)

    63	def strip_generated_sections(body: str) -> str:
    64	    """Drop machine-written ``##`` sections, keeping everything else verbatim."""
    65	    lines = body.splitlines()
    66	    out: list[str] = []

   102	        # line citations intact, and it never interpolates the text into a

     2	"""Close an issue in the local tree and run the tracking bookkeeping.
     3	
     4	Replaces ``gh issue close --reason ...`` plus the ``issues: [closed]`` half of
     5	the ``track`` job in ``.github/workflows/issue-automation.yml`` (:334-338), which
     6	fired only for ``state_reason == 'completed'``.
     7	
     8	The distinction matters more locally than it did upstream.  GitHub's sub-issue
     9	progress counted every closed child regardless of reason
    10	(issue-automation.yml:392-396); the local counter in ``track.py`` counts only
    11	children that are closed *and* completed, so an issue closed as ``not-planned``
    12	withdraws from the denominator's numerator rather than silently advancing a
    13	tracking parent toward its "ready to close" note.  Accordingly this script
    14	writes ``state_reason`` on every close and invokes ``track.py`` only for
    15	``completed``.
    16	
    17	Usage:
    18	    issue_close.py 0042 --reason completed
    19	    issue_close.py 0042 --reason not-planned --note "superseded by #0051"
    20	    issue_close.py --help
    21	"""
    22	
    23	from __future__ import annotations
    24	
    25	import argparse
    26	import sys
    27	from pathlib import Path
    28	
    29	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    30	try:
    31	    import track
    32	except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
    33	    sys.stderr.write(
    34	        "issue_close.py: cannot import local/bin/track.py, which holds the issue "
    35	        f"data layer ({exc}).\n"
    36	    )
    37	    raise SystemExit(2)
    38	
    39	from track import LayerError  # noqa: E402
    40	
    41	
    42	REASONS = ("completed", "not-planned")
    43	
    44	
    45	def close_issue(
    46	    repo_root: Path,
    47	    issue_id: str,
    48	    reason: str,
    49	    *,
    50	    note: str | None,
    51	    force: bool,
    52	    dry_run: bool,
    53	    run_track: bool = True,
    54	) -> int:
    55	    """Set ``state``/``state_reason``, append one activity note, then track.
    56	
    57	    Callable from ``pr_merge.py`` with ``run_track=False`` so the caller can
    58	    order the tracking calls itself; see the double-fire note there.
    59	    """
    60	    with track.issue_lock(issue_id):
    61	        issue = track.load_issue(repo_root, issue_id)
    62	        if issue.state == "closed" and not force:
    63	            sys.stderr.write(
    64	                f"#{issue_id} is already closed "
    65	                f"(state_reason: {issue.state_reason}); nothing to do. "
    66	                "Pass --force to rewrite the reason.\n"
    67	            )
    68	            return 0
    69	
    70	        outstanding = [
    71	            child for child in issue.children
    72	            if (loaded := track.try_load_issue(repo_root, child)) is not None
    73	            and loaded.state == "open"
    74	        ]
    75	        if outstanding:
    76	            sys.stderr.write(
    77	                f"warning: #{issue_id} still has open children "
    78	                f"({', '.join('#' + c for c in outstanding)}); closing the parent "
    79	                "does not close them.\n"
    80	            )
    81	
    82	        issue.meta["state"] = "closed"
    83	        issue.meta["state_reason"] = reason
    84	        if dry_run:
    85	            sys.stdout.write(
    86	                f"[dry-run] would close #{issue_id} as {reason}\n"
    87	            )
    88	        else:
    89	            issue.save()
    90	            sys.stdout.write(
    91	                f"{issue.path.name}: state=closed state_reason={reason}\n"
    92	            )

    94	        marker = f"closed as {reason}"
    95	        detail = f" — {track.sanitize(note, track.BODY_LIMIT)}" if note else ""
    96	        track.append_activity_once(
    97	            issue, marker, f"Issue {marker}{detail}.", dry_run=dry_run
    98	        )
    99	
   100	    if reason != "completed":
   101	        sys.stdout.write(
   102	            "state_reason is not 'completed': skipping tracking bookkeeping, so "
   103	            "this issue does not count toward its parent's progress.\n"
   104	        )
   105	        return 0
   106	
   107	    if not run_track:
   108	        return 0
   109	
   110	    return track.on_issue_state_change(repo_root, issue_id, "closed", dry_run=dry_run)

   120	    parser.add_argument("--reason", required=True, choices=REASONS,
   121	                        help="'completed' counts toward tracking progress; "
   122	                             "'not-planned' does not")
   123	    parser.add_argument("--note", default=None,
   124	                        help="one-line reason recorded in the activity log")
   125	    parser.add_argument("--force", action="store_true",
   126	                        help="rewrite state_reason on an already-closed issue")

     2	"""Validate the local issue tree against the invariants GitHub used to enforce.
     3	
     4	On GitHub, four of these properties were free.  Native sub-issues guaranteed at
     5	most one parent and kept both directions of the relationship in one server-side
     6	row; the label API rejected a name that did not exist; the pin API refused a
     7	fourth pin.  In a directory of markdown files nothing enforces any of it, which
     8	is why the study of the parent workflow called out "the local tree needs a
     9	validator for parent-child symmetry and acyclicity, since frontmatter has no
    10	server enforcing it".  This is that validator.
    11	
    12	Checks:
    13	
    14	* every ``issues/NNNN-slug.md`` parses, and its ``id`` matches its filename;
    15	* ids are unique and slugs are lowercase-kebab and bracket-free
    16	  (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124);
    17	* ``parent`` is a scalar, not a list — one parent maximum, GitHub's native
    18	  sub-issue invariant;
    19	* ``parent``/``children`` are symmetric in both directions and every referenced
    20	  id exists;
    21	* the parent relation is acyclic;
    22	* labels are a subset of ``local/labels.yml``, and none appear in its ``banned``
    23	  block (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:217-219, 292-294);
    24	* at most three issues are pinned (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:224-228);
    25	* ``state``/``state_reason`` agree: closed issues carry a reason, open ones do
    26	  not — ``track.py`` counts only ``completed`` toward tracking progress, so a
    27	  closed issue with a null reason would silently stall a parent's counter.
    28	
    29	Report-only: it never edits an issue.  Exit status is 0 when clean, 1 when any
    30	error is found, 2 on a usage or parse failure.
    31	
    32	Usage:
    33	    validate_tree.py
    34	    validate_tree.py --format json
    35	    validate_tree.py --strict          # warnings become errors
    36	    validate_tree.py --help
    37	"""
    38	
    39	from __future__ import annotations
    40	
    41	import argparse
    42	import json
    43	import re
    44	import sys
    45	from pathlib import Path
    46	
    47	sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))
    48	try:
    49	    import track
    50	except ModuleNotFoundError as exc:  # pragma: no cover - defensive
    51	    sys.stderr.write(
    52	        "validate_tree.py: cannot import local/bin/track.py, which holds the "
    53	        f"issue data layer ({exc}).\n"
    54	    )

    56	
    57	from track import LayerError  # noqa: E402
    58	
    59	
    60	MAX_PINNED = 3
    61	VALID_STATES = ("open", "closed")
    62	VALID_REASONS = ("completed", "not-planned")
    63	
    64	
    65	class Findings:
    66	    def __init__(self) -> None:
    67	        self.errors: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    68	        self.warnings: list[dict[str, str]] = []
    69	
    70	    def error(self, where: str, check: str, message: str) -> None:
    71	        self.errors.append({"where": where, "check": check, "message": message})
    72	
    73	    def warn(self, where: str, check: str, message: str) -> None:
    74	        self.warnings.append({"where": where, "check": check, "message": message})
    75	
    76	
    77	def _check_file_naming(path: Path, meta: dict, findings: Findings) -> str | None:
    78	    match = track.ISSUE_FILE_RE.match(path.name)
    79	    if not match:
    80	        findings.error(
    81	            path.name, "naming",
    82	            "filename must be NNNN-slug.md with a 4-digit id and a lowercase-kebab, "
    83	            "bracket-free slug (docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:122-124)",
    84	        )
    85	        return None
    86	    file_id = match.group(1)
    87	    meta_id = str(meta.get("id", ""))
    88	    if meta_id != file_id:
    89	        findings.error(
    90	            path.name, "naming",
    91	            f"frontmatter id {meta_id!r} does not match the filename id {file_id!r}",
    92	        )

    96	def _check_scalar_fields(issue: track.Issue, findings: Findings) -> None:
    97	    where = issue.path.name

    99	        if field not in issue.meta:

   103	    if state not in VALID_STATES:
   104	        findings.error(where, "state", f"state is {state!r}; expected one of {VALID_STATES}")

   106	    if state == "closed":
   107	        if reason not in VALID_REASONS:
   108	            findings.error(
   109	                where, "state",
   110	                f"closed issue has state_reason {reason!r}; expected one of "
   111	                f"{VALID_REASONS}. track.py counts only 'completed' toward a "
   112	                "tracking parent's progress, so a null reason stalls the counter.",
   113	            )
   114	    elif reason is not None:
   115	        findings.error(
   116	            where, "state",
   117	            f"open issue carries state_reason {reason!r}; it must be null",
   118	        )
   119	
   120	    if not isinstance(issue.meta.get("pinned"), bool):
   121	        findings.error(
   122	            where, "schema",

   124	        )
   125	    if not isinstance(issue.meta.get("labels") or [], list):
   126	        findings.error(where, "schema", "labels must be a list")
   127	    if not isinstance(issue.meta.get("children") or [], list):
   128	        findings.error(where, "schema", "children must be a list")

   130	    title = str(issue.meta.get("title") or "")
   131	    if not title.strip():
   132	        findings.error(where, "schema", "title is empty")

   134	        track.check_bracket_free(title, "title")

   136	        findings.error(where, "bracket-free", str(exc).splitlines()[0])

   168	def _check_links(issues: dict[str, track.Issue], findings: Findings) -> None:
   169	    for ident, issue in issues.items():
   170	        where = issue.path.name
   171	
   172	        try:
   173	            parent_id = issue.parent
   174	        except LayerError as exc:
   175	            findings.error(where, "one-parent", str(exc))
   176	            continue
   177	
   178	        if parent_id is not None:
   179	            if parent_id == ident:
   180	                findings.error(where, "one-parent", "issue is its own parent")
   181	            elif parent_id not in issues:
   182	                findings.error(
   183	                    where, "dangling-parent",
   184	                    f"parent #{parent_id} has no issue file",
   185	                )
   186	            elif ident not in issues[parent_id].children:
   187	                findings.error(
   188	                    where, "symmetry",
   189	                    f"#{ident} names parent #{parent_id}, but #{parent_id} does not "
   190	                    f"list #{ident} in children. Both halves must be written; "
   191	                    "issue_new.py --parent does that.",
   192	                )
   193	
   194	        seen: set[str] = set()
   195	        for child_id in issue.children:
   196	            if child_id in seen:
   197	                findings.error(where, "duplicate-child", f"child #{child_id} listed twice")
   198	                continue
   199	            seen.add(child_id)
   200	            if child_id == ident:
   201	                findings.error(where, "one-parent", "issue is its own child")
   202	                continue
   203	            child = issues.get(child_id)
   204	            if child is None:
   205	                findings.error(
   206	                    where, "dangling-child", f"child #{child_id} has no issue file"
   207	                )
   208	                continue
   209	            try:
   210	                child_parent = child.parent
   211	            except LayerError:
   212	                continue
   213	            if child_parent != ident:
   214	                findings.error(
   215	                    where, "symmetry",
   216	                    f"#{ident} lists child #{child_id}, but #{child_id} has parent "
   217	                    f"{('#' + child_parent) if child_parent else 'null'}. An issue "
   218	                    "has at most one parent, so the two records disagree.",
   219	                )

   222	def _check_acyclic(issues: dict[str, track.Issue], findings: Findings) -> None:
   223	    """Walk parent links; report the first cycle reached from each start."""
   224	    state: dict[str, int] = {}  # 0 = visiting, 1 = done
   225	
   226	    for start in issues:
   227	        if state.get(start) == 1:
   228	            continue
   229	        path: list[str] = []
   230	        node: str | None = start
   231	        while node is not None and state.get(node) != 1:
   232	            if node in path:
   233	                cycle = path[path.index(node):] + [node]
   234	                findings.error(
   235	                    issues[node].path.name, "cycle",
   236	                    "parent chain forms a cycle: " + " -> ".join("#" + n for n in cycle),
   237	                )
   238	                break
   239	            path.append(node)
   240	            state[node] = 0
   241	            current = issues.get(node)
   242	            if current is None:
   243	                break
   244	            try:
   245	                node = current.parent
   246	            except LayerError:
   247	                break
   248	            if node is not None and node not in issues:
   249	                break
   250	        for node_id in path:
   251	            state[node_id] = 1

   254	def _check_pins(issues: dict[str, track.Issue], findings: Findings) -> None:
   255	    pinned = [i for i in issues.values() if i.meta.get("pinned") is True]
   256	    if len(pinned) > MAX_PINNED:
   257	        findings.error(
   258	            "issues/", "pinned",
   259	            f"{len(pinned)} issues are pinned ("
   260	            + ", ".join("#" + i.id for i in sorted(pinned, key=lambda x: x.id))

   262	        )

   265	def _check_prs(repo_root: Path, issues: dict[str, track.Issue],
   266	               taxonomy: track.Taxonomy, findings: Findings) -> None:
   267	    """Light consistency pass over the PR registry."""
   268	    for pr in track.iter_prs(repo_root):
   269	        where = str(pr.path.parent.name) + "/pr.md"
   270	        for field in track.PR_FIELDS:
   271	            if field not in pr.meta:
   272	                findings.error(where, "schema", f"missing frontmatter field {field!r}")

   274	            findings.error(
   275	                where, "state",
   276	                f"state is {pr.meta.get('state')!r}; expected open, merged, or closed",
   277	            )

   279	        if issue_id and issue_id not in issues:
   280	            findings.error(where, "dangling-issue", f"issue #{issue_id} has no file")
   281	        branch = pr.branch
   282	        if branch:
   283	            match = re.search(r"issue-(\d+)", branch)
   284	            if not match:
   285	                findings.error(
   286	                    where, "branch",
   287	                    f"branch {branch!r} does not embed 'issue-<id>'; track.py's "
   288	                    "issue-(\\d+) regex cannot recover the link "
   289	                    "(DESIGN.md:106-107)",
   290	                )
   291	            elif issue_id and track.normalize_id(match.group(1)) != issue_id:
   292	                findings.error(
   293	                    where, "branch",
   294	                    f"branch {branch!r} embeds a different issue than "
   295	                    f"frontmatter's #{issue_id}",
   296	                )
   297	            try:
   298	                track.check_bracket_free(branch, "branch", track.FORBIDDEN_REF_CHARS)
   299	            except LayerError as exc:
   300	                findings.error(where, "bracket-free", str(exc).splitlines()[0])

   302	            if name in taxonomy.banned:
   303	                findings.error(where, "label-banned",
   304	                               f"label {name!r} is banned: {taxonomy.banned[name]}")
   305	            elif name not in taxonomy:
   306	                findings.error(where, "label-unknown",
   307	                               f"label {name!r} is not defined in local/labels.yml")

   309	
   310	def validate(repo_root: Path, *, include_prs: bool) -> Findings:
   311	    findings = Findings()
   312	    taxonomy = track.load_taxonomy(repo_root)
   313	
   314	    directory = track.issues_dir(repo_root)
   315	    if not directory.is_dir():
   316	        raise LayerError(
   317	            f"no issue tree at {directory}. Create the first issue with "
   318	            "local/bin/issue_new.py; there is nothing to validate yet."
   319	        )
   320	
   321	    issues: dict[str, track.Issue] = {}
   322	    for path in sorted(directory.glob("*.md")):
   323	        try:
   324	            meta, body = track.split_frontmatter(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   325	        except LayerError as exc:
   326	            findings.error(path.name, "parse", str(exc))
   327	            continue
   328	        issue = track.Issue(path, meta, body)
   329	        file_id = _check_file_naming(path, meta, findings)
   330	        ident = file_id or str(meta.get("id", path.stem))
   331	        if ident in issues:
   332	            findings.error(
   333	                path.name, "duplicate-id",
   334	                f"id {ident} is also used by {issues[ident].path.name}",
   335	            )
   336	            continue
   337	        issues[ident] = issue
   338	
   339	    for issue in issues.values():
   340	        _check_scalar_fields(issue, findings)
   341	        _check_labels(issue, taxonomy, findings)
   342	
   343	    _check_links(issues, findings)
   344	    _check_acyclic(issues, findings)
   345	    _check_pins(issues, findings)
   346	    if include_prs:
   347	        _check_prs(repo_root, issues, taxonomy, findings)
   348	
   349	    findings.scanned = len(issues)  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
   350	    return findings
   351	
   352	
   353	def render_text(findings: Findings) -> str:
   354	    lines = [f"scanned {getattr(findings, 'scanned', 0)} issue file(s)"]
   355	    for kind, rows in (("ERROR", findings.errors), ("warning", findings.warnings)):
   356	        for row in rows:
   357	            lines.append(f"{kind} {row['where']} [{row['check']}] {row['message']}")
   358	    if not findings.errors and not findings.warnings:
   359	        lines.append("tree is consistent")
   360	    else:
   361	        lines.append(
   362	            f"{len(findings.errors)} error(s), {len(findings.warnings)} warning(s)"
   363	        )
   364	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   365	
   366	
   367	def render_json(findings: Findings) -> str:
   368	    return json.dumps(
   369	        {
   370	            "scanned": getattr(findings, "scanned", 0),
   371	            "errors": findings.errors,
   372	            "warnings": findings.warnings,
   373	            "ok": not findings.errors,
   374	        },
   375	        indent=2,
   376	    ) + "\n"
   377	
   378	
   379	def _parse_args(argv: list[str]) -> argparse.Namespace:
   380	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
   381	        prog="validate_tree.py",
   382	        description=__doc__,
   383	        formatter_class=argparse.RawDescriptionHelpFormatter,
   384	    )
   385	    parser.add_argument("--repo-root", type=Path, default=track.default_repo_root(),
   386	                        help="repository root (default: two levels above this script)")
   387	    parser.add_argument("--format", choices=("text", "json"), default="text",
   388	                        help="output format (default: text)")
   389	    parser.add_argument("--output", type=Path,
   390	                        help="write the report here instead of stdout")
   391	    parser.add_argument("--no-prs", action="store_true",
   392	                        help="skip the PR registry consistency pass")
   393	    parser.add_argument("--strict", action="store_true",
   394	                        help="treat warnings as errors")
   395	    return parser.parse_args(argv)
   396	
   397	
   398	def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
   399	    args = _parse_args(sys.argv[1:] if argv is None else argv)
   400	    try:
   401	        findings = validate(args.repo_root.resolve(), include_prs=not args.no_prs)
   402	    except LayerError as exc:
   403	        sys.stderr.write(f"validate_tree.py: {exc}\n")
   404	        return 2
   405	    rendered = render_json(findings) if args.format == "json" else render_text(findings)
   406	    if args.output:
   407	        track.atomic_write(args.output, rendered)
   408	        sys.stdout.write(f"wrote {args.output}\n")
   409	    else:
   410	        sys.stdout.write(rendered)
   411	    if findings.errors or (args.strict and findings.warnings):
   412	        return 1
   413	    return 0
   414	
   415	
   416	if __name__ == "__main__":
   417	    raise SystemExit(main())

item.text: The direct executable set is now clear: the registry core is `track.py`, with issue/PR lifecycle tools layered on it; CI, review, auto-fix, merge, agent dispatch, and housekeeping all consume its records. I’m reading each boundary now to separate code that must be rewritten from registry-only machinery that should be retired, and to preserve reusable invariants such as branch safety, exact-head checks, and sanitization.

   175	    groups are per-cause: "an opened-issue run and the label events that
   176	    classification fires moments later must not cancel one another").  Locally
   177	    the analogous hazard is two agent sessions mutating the same issue file;
   178	    a per-entity ``flock`` plus the atomic writer below covers it.
   179	
   180	    Re-entrant within one process so a caller may hold an issue lock while a
   181	    helper re-acquires it.
   182	    """
   183	    if _HELD.get(name):
   184	        _HELD[name] += 1
   185	        try:
   186	            yield
   187	        finally:
   188	            _HELD[name] -= 1
   189	        return
   190	
   191	    directory = lock_dir()
   192	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   193	    path = directory / f"{name}.lock"
   194	    fd = os.open(str(path), os.O_CREAT | os.O_RDWR, 0o644)
   195	    try:
   196	        try:
   197	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX | fcntl.LOCK_NB)
   198	        except OSError as exc:
   199	            if exc.errno not in (errno.EAGAIN, errno.EACCES):
   200	                raise
   201	            sys.stderr.write(f"waiting for lock {path} ...\n")
   202	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)
   203	        os.ftruncate(fd, 0)
   204	        os.write(fd, f"{os.getpid()}\n".encode())
   205	        _HELD[name] = 1
   206	        try:
   207	            yield
   208	        finally:
   209	            _HELD.pop(name, None)
   210	            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)
   211	    finally:
   212	        os.close(fd)
   213	
   214	
   215	def issue_lock(issue_id: str):
   216	    return file_lock(f"issue-{issue_id}")
   217	
   218	
   219	def pr_lock(pr_id: str):
   220	    return file_lock(f"pr-{pr_id}")

   226	
   227	def atomic_write(path: Path, text: str) -> None:
   228	    """Write *text* to *path* via tempfile + ``os.replace``.
   229	
   230	    Every frontmatter mutation goes through here.  A half-written issue file is
   231	    worse than a lost one: the tree is the only record of parent/child structure
   232	    and there is no server to reconstruct it.
   233	    """
   234	    path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   235	    fd, tmp = tempfile.mkstemp(dir=str(path.parent), prefix=f".{path.name}.", suffix=".tmp")
   236	    try:
   237	        with os.fdopen(fd, "w", encoding="utf-8") as handle:
   238	            handle.write(text)
   239	            handle.flush()
   240	            os.fsync(handle.fileno())
   241	        os.replace(tmp, path)
   242	    except BaseException:
   243	        try:
   244	            os.unlink(tmp)
   245	        except OSError:
   246	            pass
   247	        raise
   248	    dir_fd = os.open(str(path.parent), os.O_RDONLY)
   249	    try:
   250	        os.fsync(dir_fd)
   251	    finally:
   252	        os.close(dir_fd)

   255	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   256	# A deliberately small YAML subset
   257	# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
   258	#
   259	# Scope: scalars (string / int / bool / null), ``[a, b]`` flow sequences, block
   260	# sequences of scalars or of mappings, two-space indentation, full-line ``#``
   261	# comments.  Everything this layer writes stays inside that subset, and
   262	# labels.yml is authored to match.  Anything richer should be rejected loudly
   263	# rather than half-understood.
   264	
   265	_KEY_RE = re.compile(r"^(?P<key>[A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9_.\- ]*):(?:[ \t]+(?P<val>.*))?$")
   266	
   267	
   268	def _parse_scalar(raw: str | None) -> object:
   269	    if raw is None:
   270	        return None
   271	    text = raw.strip()
   272	    if text == "" or text in {"null", "~"}:
   273	        return None
   274	    if text in {"true", "True"}:
   275	        return True
   276	    if text in {"false", "False"}:
   277	        return False
   278	    if text.startswith("[") and text.endswith("]"):
   279	        return _parse_flow_list(text[1:-1])
   280	    if len(text) >= 2 and text[0] == text[-1] and text[0] in "\"'":
   281	        return _unquote(text)
   282	    if re.fullmatch(r"-?\d+", text):
   283	        return int(text)
   284	    return text
   285	
   286	
   287	def _unquote(text: str) -> str:
   288	    quote = text[0]
   289	    inner = text[1:-1]
   290	    if quote == "'":
   291	        return inner.replace("''", "'")
   292	    out: list[str] = []
   293	    escaped = False
   294	    for ch in inner:
   295	        if escaped:
   296	            out.append({"n": "\n", "t": "\t"}.get(ch, ch))
   297	            escaped = False
   298	        elif ch == "\\":
   299	            escaped = True
   300	        else:
   301	            out.append(ch)
   302	    return "".join(out)
   303	
   304	
   305	def _parse_flow_list(inner: str) -> list[object]:
   306	    items: list[object] = []
   307	    buf: list[str] = []
   308	    quote: str | None = None
   309	    escaped = False
   310	    for ch in inner:
   311	        if escaped:
   312	            buf.append(ch)
   313	            escaped = False
   314	            continue
   315	        if quote:
   316	            buf.append(ch)
   317	            if ch == "\\" and quote == '"':
   318	                escaped = True
   319	            elif ch == quote:
   320	                quote = None
   321	            continue
   322	        if ch in "\"'":
   323	            quote = ch
   324	            buf.append(ch)
   325	            continue
   326	        if ch == ",":
   327	            items.append("".join(buf))
   328	            buf = []
   329	            continue
   330	        buf.append(ch)
   331	    if "".join(buf).strip():
   332	        items.append("".join(buf))
   333	    return [_parse_scalar(item) for item in items if item.strip() != ""]
   334	
   335	
   336	def _significant(lines: Sequence[str]) -> list[tuple[int, str, int]]:
   337	    """(indent, text, source_line_number) for non-blank, non-comment lines."""
   338	    out: list[tuple[int, str, int]] = []
   339	    for number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
   340	        if "\t" in line[: len(line) - len(line.lstrip())]:
   341	            raise LayerError(f"line {number}: tab indentation is not supported")
   342	        stripped = line.strip()
   343	        if not stripped or stripped.startswith("#"):
   344	            continue
   345	        out.append((len(line) - len(line.lstrip(" ")), stripped, number))
   346	    return out
   347	
   348	
   349	def _parse_block(rows: list[tuple[int, str, int]], index: int, indent: int) -> tuple[object, int]:
   350	    if index >= len(rows):
   351	        return None, index
   352	    if rows[index][1].startswith("- "):
   353	        return _parse_sequence(rows, index, indent)
   354	    return _parse_mapping(rows, index, indent)
   355	
   356	
   357	def _parse_mapping(rows, index: int, indent: int) -> tuple[dict, int]:
   358	    result: dict[str, object] = {}
   359	    while index < len(rows):
   360	        level, text, number = rows[index]
   361	        if level < indent:
   362	            break
   363	        if level > indent:
   364	            raise LayerError(f"line {number}: unexpected indentation in mapping")
   365	        match = _KEY_RE.match(text)
   366	        if not match:
   367	            raise LayerError(f"line {number}: not a supported mapping entry: {text!r}")
   368	        key = match.group("key").strip()
   369	        raw = match.group("val")
   370	        index += 1
   371	        if raw is None or raw.strip() == "":
   372	            if index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] > indent:
   373	                value, index = _parse_block(rows, index, rows[index][0])
   374	            elif index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] == indent and rows[index][1].startswith("- "):
   375	                value, index = _parse_sequence(rows, index, indent)
   376	            else:
   377	                value = None
   378	        else:
   379	            value = _parse_scalar(raw)
   380	        result[key] = value
   381	    return result, index
   382	
   383	
   384	def _parse_sequence(rows, index: int, indent: int) -> tuple[list, int]:
   385	    items: list[object] = []
   386	    while index < len(rows):
   387	        level, text, number = rows[index]
   388	        if level < indent or not text.startswith("- "):
   389	            break
   390	        if level > indent:
   391	            raise LayerError(f"line {number}: unexpected indentation in sequence")
   392	        payload = text[2:].strip()
   393	        index += 1
   394	        if _KEY_RE.match(payload):
   395	            child_indent = level + 2
   396	            sub_rows: list[tuple[int, str, int]] = [(child_indent, payload, number)]
   397	            while index < len(rows) and rows[index][0] >= child_indent and not (
   398	                rows[index][0] == level and rows[index][1].startswith("- ")
   399	            ):
   400	                if rows[index][0] < child_indent:

401	                    break
   402	                sub_rows.append((child_indent, rows[index][1], rows[index][2])
   403	                                if rows[index][0] == child_indent else rows[index])
   404	                index += 1
   405	            mapping, _ = _parse_mapping(sub_rows, 0, child_indent)
   406	            items.append(mapping)
   407	        else:
   408	            items.append(_parse_scalar(payload))
   409	    return items, index
   410	
   411	
   412	def parse_yaml_subset(text: str) -> dict:
   413	    rows = _significant(text.splitlines())
   414	    if not rows:
   415	        return {}
   416	    value, _ = _parse_mapping(rows, 0, rows[0][0])
   417	    return value
   418	
   419	
   420	def _emit_scalar(value: object) -> str:
   421	    if value is None:
   422	        return "null"
   423	    if isinstance(value, bool):
   424	        return "true" if value else "false"
   425	    if isinstance(value, int):
   426	        return str(value)
   427	    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
   428	        return "[" + ", ".join(_emit_scalar(v) for v in value) + "]"
   429	    escaped = str(value).replace("\\", "\\\\").replace('"', '\\"')
   430	    escaped = escaped.replace("\n", "\\n").replace("\r", "")
   431	    return f'"{escaped}"'
   432	
   433	
   434	def dump_frontmatter(meta: dict, order: Sequence[str]) -> str:
   435	    """Serialize *meta* in *order*; unknown keys follow, sorted, for visibility."""
   436	    keys = list(order) + sorted(k for k in meta if k not in order)
   437	    lines = ["---"]
   438	    for key in keys:
   439	        if key not in meta:
   440	            continue
   441	        lines.append(f"{key}: {_emit_scalar(meta[key])}")
   442	    lines.append("---")
   443	    return "\n".join(lines) + "\n"
   444	
   445	
   446	def split_frontmatter(text: str) -> tuple[dict, str]:
   447	    """Return ``(frontmatter, body)``; raises when the fence is missing."""
   448	    if not text.startswith("---"):
   449	        raise LayerError("file does not start with a '---' frontmatter fence")
   450	    lines = text.splitlines()
   451	    end = None
   452	    for number in range(1, len(lines)):
   453	        if lines[number].strip() == "---":
   454	            end = number
   455	            break
   456	    if end is None:
   457	        raise LayerError("unterminated frontmatter: no closing '---'")
   458	    meta = parse_yaml_subset("\n".join(lines[1:end]))
   459	    body = "\n".join(lines[end + 1:])
   460	    return meta, body.lstrip("\n")

   467	class Taxonomy:
   468	    """Parsed ``local/labels.yml``: the local replacement for ``gh label list``."""
   469	
   470	    def __init__(self, names: list[str], entries: list[dict], banned: dict[str, str]):
   471	        self.names = names
   472	        self.entries = entries
   473	        self.banned = banned
   474	
   475	    def __contains__(self, name: object) -> bool:
   476	        return name in self.names
   477	
   478	    def aliases_by_label(self) -> dict[str, list[str]]:
   479	        out: dict[str, list[str]] = {}
   480	        for entry in self.entries:
   481	            aliases = entry.get("aliases") or []
   482	            if isinstance(aliases, list) and aliases:
   483	                out[str(entry["name"])] = [str(a).lower() for a in aliases]
   484	        return out
   485	
   486	    def by_category(self, category: str) -> list[str]:
   487	        return [str(e["name"]) for e in self.entries if e.get("category") == category]

   489	
   490	def load_taxonomy(repo_root: Path) -> Taxonomy:
   491	    path = repo_root / "local" / "labels.yml"
   492	    if not path.is_file():
   493	        raise LayerError(
   494	            f"label taxonomy not found at {path}. It is the local source of truth "
   495	            "for labels (replacing 'GitHub is the source of truth', "
   496	            "docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:286-289) and is required before any issue may "
   497	            "be created or validated."
   498	        )
   499	    data = parse_yaml_subset(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
   500	    entries = data.get("labels") or []
   501	    if not isinstance(entries, list) or not entries:
   502	        raise LayerError(f"{path}: 'labels:' must be a non-empty block sequence")
   503	    names: list[str] = []
   504	    for entry in entries:
   505	        if not isinstance(entry, dict) or "name" not in entry:
   506	            raise LayerError(f"{path}: every label entry needs a 'name' key")
   507	        names.append(str(entry["name"]))
   508	    banned = {}
   509	    for entry in data.get("banned") or []:
   510	        if isinstance(entry, dict) and "name" in entry:
   511	            banned[str(entry["name"])] = str(entry.get("reason", "banned"))
   512	    return Taxonomy(names, [e for e in entries if isinstance(e, dict)], banned)

   736	    The counter file is authoritative but is reconciled against the ids already
   737	    on disk on every allocation: a counter restored from an older commit must
   738	    never hand out an id that is already taken.  Callers hold the sequence lock.
   739	    """
   740	    highest = 0
   741	    for value in existing:
   742	        try:
   743	            highest = max(highest, int(value))
   744	        except (TypeError, ValueError):
   745	            continue
   746	    current = 0
   747	    if seq_path.is_file():
   748	        raw = seq_path.read_text(encoding="utf-8").strip()
   749	        if raw:
   750	            if not raw.isdigit():
   751	                raise LayerError(f"{seq_path}: expected a decimal counter, found {raw!r}")
   752	            current = int(raw)
   753	    allocated = max(current, highest) + 1
   754	    atomic_write(seq_path, f"{allocated}\n")
   755	    return f"{allocated:04d}"

   762	def append_activity_once(issue: Issue, marker: str, note: str, *, dry_run: bool = False) -> bool:
   763	    """Append one ``## Activity`` bullet unless *marker* already appears.
   764	
   765	    Direct port of ``commentOnce`` (issue-automation.yml:403-417).  The parent
   766	    scanned every existing comment body for the marker substring; here the whole
   767	    issue file plays that role.  Returns True when the note was written.
   768	
   769	    ``## Activity`` is the terminal section of an issue file by convention, so
   770	    the append is a plain end-of-file write and never has to reflow the body.
   771	    """
   772	    with issue_lock(issue.id):
   773	        current = issue.path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   774	        if marker in current:
   775	            return False
   776	        meta, body = split_frontmatter(current)
   777	        fresh = Issue(issue.path, meta, body)
   778	        text = fresh.body.rstrip("\n")
   779	        if ACTIVITY_HEADING not in text:
   780	            text += f"\n\n{ACTIVITY_HEADING}\n"
   781	        if text.rstrip("\n").endswith(ACTIVITY_HEADING):
   782	            text = text.rstrip("\n") + "\n"
   783	        text += f"\n- {utcnow()} — {note}"
   784	        fresh.body = text
   785	        if dry_run:
   786	            sys.stdout.write(f"[dry-run] {issue.path.name}: {note}\n")
   787	            return True
   788	        fresh.save()
   789	        issue.meta = fresh.meta
   790	        issue.body = fresh.body
   791	        sys.stdout.write(f"{issue.path.name}: {note}\n")
   792	        return True

   197	)

   206	def classify_deterministic(title: str, body: str, taxonomy: track.Taxonomy) -> list[str]:
   207	    """Keyword labels for *title*/*body*, filtered against the taxonomy.
   208	
   209	    The filtering step is the local form of issue-automation.yml:172-179
   210	    ("Fetch existing repo labels so we don't fail on nonexistent labels"): a
   211	    proposed label that ``local/labels.yml`` does not define is dropped with a
   212	    note rather than written into frontmatter, where it would then fail
   213	    ``validate_tree.py``.
   214	
   215	    The parent hard-coded its chapter regex (``wolf-ch[1-7]``) and its paper-id
   216	    list inline; both had drifted away from the live taxonomy by the time of the
   217	    study.  Here the family and paper labels come from ``aliases:`` entries in
   218	    ``local/labels.yml``, so there is exactly one place to edit.
   219	    """
   220	    text = f"{title}\n{body}".lower()
   221	    proposed: list[str] = []
   222	
   223	    def add(name: str) -> None:
   224	        if name not in proposed:
   225	            proposed.append(name)
   226	
   227	    if _FORMALIZATION_RE.search(text):
   228	        add("formalization")
   229	    if _DOCUMENTATION_RE.search(text):
   230	        add("documentation")
   231	    if _BUG_RE.search(text):
   232	        add("bug")
   233	    if _CI_RE.search(text):
   234	        add("ci")
   235	    if _TRACKING_TITLE_RE.search(title.lower()):
   236	        add("tracking")
   237	
   238	    for label, aliases in taxonomy.aliases_by_label().items():
   239	        if any(alias in text for alias in aliases):
   240	            add(label)
   241	
   242	    valid = [name for name in proposed if name in taxonomy]
   243	    dropped = [name for name in proposed if name not in taxonomy]
   244	    for name in dropped:
   245	        sys.stderr.write(
   246	            f"note: dropping proposed label {name!r}: not defined in local/labels.yml\n"
   247	        )
   248	    return sorted(valid)

   338	def resolve_labels(requested: list[str], template: str, taxonomy: track.Taxonomy) -> list[str]:

   359	def attach_to_parent(repo_root: Path, parent_id: str, child_id: str, *, dry_run: bool) -> None:
   360	    """Write the parent half of the relationship under the parent's lock."""
   361	    with track.issue_lock(parent_id):
   362	        parent = track.load_issue(repo_root, parent_id)
   363	        if parent.state != "open":
   364	            sys.stderr.write(
   365	                f"warning: parent #{parent_id} is {parent.state}; attaching anyway\n"
   366	            )
   367	        children = parent.children
   368	        if child_id in children:
   369	            return
   370	        children.append(child_id)
   371	        parent.meta["children"] = sorted(children)
   372	        if dry_run:
   373	            sys.stdout.write(f"[dry-run] would add #{child_id} to #{parent_id}.children\n")
   374	            return
   375	        parent.save()
   376	        sys.stdout.write(f"#{parent_id}: children now {parent.meta['children']}\n")

   379	def create_issue(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:
   380	    repo_root = args.repo_root.resolve()
   381	    taxonomy = track.load_taxonomy(repo_root)
   382	
   383	    title = track.sanitize(args.title, track.TITLE_LIMIT).strip()
   384	    if not title:
   385	        raise LayerError("--title is empty after sanitization")
   386	    track.check_bracket_free(title, "issue title")
   387	    slug = track.slugify(title)
   388	
   389	    labels = resolve_labels(args.labels, args.template, taxonomy)
   390	
   391	    parent_id = track.normalize_id(args.parent) if args.parent else None
   392	    if parent_id is not None:
   393	        # Fail before allocating an id if the parent does not exist.
   394	        track.load_issue(repo_root, parent_id)
   395	
   396	    if args.pinned:
   397	        pinned = [i for i in track.iter_issues(repo_root) if i.meta.get("pinned") is True]
   398	        if len(pinned) >= 3:
   399	            raise LayerError(
   400	                f"{len(pinned)} issue(s) are already pinned "
   401	                f"({', '.join('#' + i.id for i in pinned)}); the cap is 3 "
   402	                "(docs/CONTRIBUTING.md:224-228) and validate_tree.py enforces it. "
   403	                "Unpin one first."
   404	            )
   405	
   406	    directory = track.issues_dir(repo_root)
   407	    directory.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
   408	
   409	    with track.file_lock("issues-seq"):
   410	        existing = [i.id for i in track.iter_issues(repo_root)]
   411	        if args.dry_run:
   412	            issue_id = f"{(max([int(e) for e in existing], default=0) + 1):04d}"
   413	        else:
   414	            issue_id = track.next_sequence_id(directory / ".seq", existing)
   415	
   416	    now = track.utcnow()
   417	    meta = {
   418	        "id": issue_id,
   419	        "title": title,
   420	        "state": "open",
   421	        "state_reason": None,
   422	        "parent": parent_id,
   423	        "children": [],
   424	        "labels": labels,
   425	        "pinned": bool(args.pinned),
   426	        "created": now,
   427	        "updated": now,
   428	        "agent_session": args.agent_session,
   429	    }
   430	    body = TEMPLATE_BODIES[args.template]
   431	    if args.body_file:
   432	        supplied = Path(args.body_file).read_text(encoding="utf-8")
   433	        body = track.sanitize(supplied, track.BODY_LIMIT)
   434	    body = body.rstrip("\n") + f"\n\n{track.ACTIVITY_HEADING}\n"
   435	
   436	    path = directory / f"{issue_id}-{slug}.md"
   437	    if path.exists():
   438	        raise LayerError(f"{path} already exists; refusing to overwrite")
   439	
   440	    issue = track.Issue(path, meta, body)
   441	    if args.dry_run:
   442	        sys.stdout.write(f"[dry-run] would create {path}\n\n{issue.render()}\n")
   443	        return 0
   444	
   445	    track.atomic_write(path, issue.render())
   446	    sys.stdout.write(f"created {path.relative_to(repo_root)} (#{issue_id})\n")
   447	
   448	    if parent_id is not None:
   449	        attach_to_parent(repo_root, parent_id, issue_id, dry_run=False)
   450	
   451	    # Stage 2: classification. Must complete before stage 3.
   452	    if not args.no_classify:
   453	        # An unedited template body is boilerplate, not content: its placeholder
   454	        # prose names "blueprint", "theorem", "build" and would classify every
   455	        # new issue identically. Only a body the caller actually supplied joins
   456	        # the title as classification input.
   457	        source_body = body if args.body_file else ""
   458	        derived = classify_deterministic(title, source_body, taxonomy)
   459	        merged = sorted(set(labels) | set(derived))
   460	        with track.issue_lock(issue_id):
   461	            fresh = track.load_issue(repo_root, issue_id)
   462	            fresh.meta["labels"] = merged
   463	            if CLASSIFICATION_HEADING not in fresh.body:
   464	                activity = fresh.body.find(track.ACTIVITY_HEADING)
   465	                note = classification_note(derived)
   466	                if activity == -1:
   467	                    fresh.body = fresh.body.rstrip("\n") + "\n\n" + note
   468	                else:
   469	                    fresh.body = (
   470	                        fresh.body[:activity].rstrip("\n")
   471	                        + "\n\n" + note + "\n"
   472	                        + fresh.body[activity:]
   473	                    )
   474	            fresh.save()
   475	        sys.stdout.write(f"#{issue_id}: labels {merged}\n")
   476	
   477	    # Stage 3: scouting, strictly after classification.
   478	    if not args.no_scout:
   479	        maybe_scout(repo_root, issue_id)
   480	
   481	    return 0

   168	    """Refuse while the serialized fix loop is mid-flight or over its cap."""
   169	    # autofix.sh holds a mkdir-based lease directory keyed on the BRANCH
   170	    # (autofix.sh "---- lock" section: locks/fix-<branch with / -> ->.lock,
   171	    # with the holder's pid in <lock>/pid).  Probe the same lock the same way;
   172	    # a dead holder's lock does not block the merge.
   173	    branch = str(meta.get("branch", ""))
   174	    if branch:
   175	        lock = track.lock_dir() / ("fix-" + branch.replace("/", "-") + ".lock")
   176	        if lock.is_dir():
   177	            pid_text = ""
   178	            try:
   179	                pid_text = (lock / "pid").read_text(encoding="ascii").split()[0]
   180	            except (OSError, IndexError):
   181	                pass
   182	            if pid_text.isdigit() and _pid_alive(int(pid_text)):
   183	                raise GateFailure(
   184	                    f"{lock} is held by live pid {pid_text}: local/bin/autofix.sh "
   185	                    "is rewriting this branch. Merging under it would race the "
   186	                    "fix commits."
   187	                )
   188	
   189	    cap = int(os.environ.get("MIPSTARRE_FIX_CAP", DEFAULT_FIX_CAP))
   190	    iterations = meta.get("fix_iterations", 0)
   191	    if not isinstance(iterations, int):
   192	        raise GateFailure(f"fix_iterations is {iterations!r}; expected an integer")
   193	    if iterations > cap:
   194	        raise GateFailure(
   195	            f"fix_iterations is {iterations}, above the combined cap of {cap}. "
   196	            "The cap is combined across ci/blueprint/review fixes (DESIGN.md:70-72); "
   197	            "a PR past it needs human attention, not another merge attempt."
   198	        )

   201	def run_gate(repo_root: Path, record: track.PullRequest, *, allow_unreviewed: bool,
   202	             adjudicated: bool = False) -> str:
   203	    """Raise ``GateFailure`` unless the PR may merge; return the head SHA."""
   204	    meta = record.meta
   205	    record_dir = record.path.parent
   206	
   207	    if record.state != "open":
   208	        raise GateFailure(
   209	            f"PR #{record.id} is {record.state!r}, not open; nothing to merge."
   210	        )
   211	
   212	    branch = record.branch
   213	    if not branch:
   214	        raise GateFailure(f"PR #{record.id} has no branch recorded")
   215	    tip = git(repo_root, "rev-parse", "--verify", f"{branch}^{{commit}}", check=False)
   216	    if not tip:
   217	        raise GateFailure(
   218	            f"branch {branch!r} does not resolve in this repository; it may have "
   219	            "been deleted already."
   220	        )
   221	
   222	    head_sha = meta.get("head_sha")
   223	    if not head_sha:
   224	        raise GateFailure(
   225	            f"PR #{record.id} has head_sha: null. Run local/bin/ci.sh on the branch "
   226	            "so the record names the commit that was tested."
   227	        )
   228	    if str(head_sha) != tip:
   229	        raise GateFailure(
   230	            f"head_sha {str(head_sha)[:12]} does not match the branch tip "
   231	            f"{tip[:12]}. New commits landed after the recorded CI/review; re-run "
   232	            "local/bin/ci.sh and local/bin/review.sh (DESIGN.md:66-69)."
   233	        )
   234	
   235	    ci_status = meta.get("ci_status")
   236	    if ci_status != "success":
   237	        raise GateFailure(
   238	            f"ci_status is {ci_status!r}, not 'success'. Run local/bin/ci.sh "
   239	            f"{record.id} and merge only on green."
   240	        )
   241	    ci_dir = record_dir / "ci"
   242	    manifest = ci_dir / f"{head_sha}.json"
   243	    if not ci_dir.is_dir():
   244	        raise GateFailure(
   245	            f"{ci_dir} does not exist. The frontmatter claims success but there is "
   246	            "no per-SHA manifest to back it; run local/bin/ci.sh."
   247	        )
   248	    if not manifest.is_file():
   249	        raise GateFailure(
   250	            f"no CI manifest at {manifest}. ci_status in frontmatter is a summary; "
   251	            "the manifest for the exact head SHA is the evidence."
   252	        )
   253	
   254	    review_state = meta.get("review_state")
   255	    if kill_switch_disabled("LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED"):
   256	        if not allow_unreviewed:
   257	            raise GateFailure(
   258	                "LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED=false, so no verdict can be produced. The "
   259	                "gate does not silently waive review: re-enable reviews, or merge "
   260	                "with --allow-unreviewed, which records the waiver in the PR."
   261	            )
   262	        sys.stderr.write(
   263	            "warning: merging with review disabled and --allow-unreviewed given\n"
   264	        )
   265	    elif review_state == "blocked":
   266	        raise GateFailure(
   267	            "review_state is 'blocked': CI failed, so review was refused rather "
   268	            "than skipped (DESIGN.md:66-69). Fix CI first."
   269	        )
   270	    elif not review_state:
   271	        raise GateFailure(
   272	            f"PR #{record.id} has review_state: null. Run local/bin/review.sh "
   273	            f"{record.id} on the current head SHA."
   274	        )
   275	    else:
   276	        check_review_verdict(record_dir, str(head_sha), str(review_state),
   277	                             adjudicated=adjudicated)
   278	
   279	    check_fix_gates(repo_root, record_dir, meta)
   280	    return str(head_sha)

   351	
   352	    DESIGN.md:63-65: only the warmer writes the hot main cache.  Merging is the
   353	    event that invalidates it, so this is where the refresh belongs — in the
   354	    background, because the merge must not block on a build.

   840	def linked_issues(pr_body: str, branch: str) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:
   841	    """``(keep_open, auto_close)`` — port of ``linkedIssues``.
   842	
   843	    issue-automation.yml:453-478.  ``Addresses``/``Partially addresses`` keep an
   844	    issue open; ``Closes``/``Fixes`` auto-close it on merge.  The branch name
   845	    contributes a keep-open link through the ``issue-(\\d+)`` regex, which is
   846	    why DESIGN.md:106-107 fixes the branch convention as
   847	    ``issue-<id>-<slug>`` / ``codex/issue-<id>-<slug>``.
   848	
   849	    The upstream comment at issue-automation.yml:450-452 records the reason the
   850	    two sets are disjoint: "Closes/Fixes issues are excluded from progress
   851	    comments: their auto-close fires the issues/closed path, which handles the
   852	    tracking update."  Locally ``pr_merge.py`` performs the auto-close itself
   853	    and then calls the closed path, so the same exclusion prevents a doubled
   854	    note on the tracking parent.
   855	    """
   856	    keep_open: list[str] = []
   857	    auto_close: list[str] = []
   858	    for keyword, number in _LINK_RE.findall(pr_body or ""):
   859	        ident = normalize_id(number)
   860	        if keyword.lower() in {"closes", "fixes"}:
   861	            if ident not in auto_close:
   862	                auto_close.append(ident)
   863	        elif ident not in keep_open:
   864	            keep_open.append(ident)
   865	    match = _BRANCH_ISSUE_RE.search(branch or "")
   866	    if match:
   867	        ident = normalize_id(match.group(1))
   868	        if ident not in auto_close and ident not in keep_open:
   869	            keep_open.append(ident)
   870	    keep_open = [i for i in keep_open if i not in auto_close]
   871	    return keep_open, auto_close

   886	
   887	    Port of ``prReferencePattern`` (issue-automation.yml:428-436).  GitHub gave

1	# Protocol — local PR CI
     2	
     3	Normative protocol for `local/bin/ci.sh`, the local replacement for
     4	`.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml` (frozen under `.github/`, never executed here).
     5	Read `meta.md` first; `build-cache.md` owns the hot-main cache this protocol
     6	consumes but never writes.
     7	
     8	`ci.sh <pr-id>` is the **only** thing allowed to set `ci_status` in a PR
     9	record. Everything downstream — `review.sh` (invariant 2: review only after
    10	green CI on the same head SHA), `autofix.sh` (invariant 3: sync/audit failures
    11	are never auto-fixed), and the merge gate in `pr_merge.py` — reads the manifest
    12	this script writes and nothing else.
    13	
    14	## 1. What it is
    15	
    16	The parent repository consolidated seven workflows into one so that a pull
    17	request produces exactly **one** CI completion event, which the auto-fix
    18	dispatcher keys off (`pr-ci.yml:3-8`). The local port keeps that property: one
    19	invocation, one manifest, one exit code.
    20	
    21	```
    22	local/bin/ci.sh <pr-id> [--worktree PATH] [--base REF] [--only STEP]
    23	                        [--force-all] [--skip-build] [--dry-run]
    24	```
    25	
    26	`<pr-id>` is `7`, `0007`, or `0007-slug`; the script resolves it to a single
    27	directory under `prs/`, reads `branch` and `base` from `pr.md` frontmatter,
    28	finds the branch's worktree (via `git worktree list`, falling back to
    29	`.worktrees/<branch with / → ->`), and runs everything **inside that
    30	worktree**. Nothing is run in the primary checkout.
    31	
    32	Exit status: `0` all gating steps passed or were legitimately skipped; `1` at
    33	least one gating step failed or could not run; `2` the run could not start
    34	(unknown PR id, missing worktree, unresolvable base).
    35	
    36	### Preconditions that are hard errors, never silent skips
    37	
    38	| Precondition | Why it is fatal |
    39	|---|---|
    40	| `prs/<id>/pr.md` exists with a `branch` key | there is no branch to test |
    41	| a worktree for that branch exists | CI must not test the primary checkout |
    42	| `origin/<base>` or `<base>` resolves | invariant 8 — the diff-based audits and the change gating self-disable without a base, which is exactly the "checks silently stopped running" failure the parent repo patched twice |
    43	| a merge base exists | the change set is undefined without one |
    44	| `python3` on `PATH` | every audit job and the manifest writer need it |
    45	
    46	There is deliberately **no `LOCAL_CI_ENABLED` kill switch**. `LOCAL_REVIEW_ENABLED`
    47	and `LOCAL_AUTO_FIX_ENABLED` exist because a disabled reviewer or fixer merely
    48	stops work from happening; a disabled CI would hand the merge gate a green
    49	light it never earned. If CI must not run, do not run it — the record keeps its
    50	previous `ci_status`.
    51	
    52	## 2. Job table
    53	
    54	Eight steps, in this order, named exactly after the parent workflow's job ids
    55	so the auto-fix dispatcher's mapping (build → ci-fix, blueprint-render →
    56	blueprint-fix, everything else → never auto-fixed) ports without translation.
    57	
    58	| Step | Parent job | What it runs (in the worktree) | Gate |
    59	|---|---|---|---|
    60	| `build` | `build` (`pr-ci.yml:115-168`) | warm `.lake/build`, `lake exe cache get`, `lake build`, `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit` (`:155-156`), `scripts/comparator/check_challenge_drift.py` (`:158-159`) | `lean ∨ comparator ∨ workflow` |
    61	| `blueprint-render` | `blueprint-render` (`:173-243`) | `leanblueprint pdf` + non-empty `blueprint/print/print.pdf` (`:210-218`), `texra-blueprint bbl` (`:222-223`), `texra-blueprint web` with `grep '^ERROR:'` (`:225-243`) | `blueprint_src ∨ workflow` |
    62	| `paper-gaps` | `paper-gaps` (`:248-271`) | `texra-blueprint --root . paper-gaps check` | `paper_gaps ∨ workflow` |
    63	| `blueprint-sync` | `blueprint-sync` (`:273-317`) | `python3 -m unittest discover -s scripts/tests`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --update-lean-decls`, `blueprint_lean_sync.py --ci`, `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py --base-ref` | `lean ∨ blueprint ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
    64	| `file-length` | `file-length` (`:319-340`) | `check_oversized_lean_files.py --root .` (>1000 lines) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
    65	| `proof-debt` | `proof-debt` (`:342-386`) | `unittest test_audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py`, `audit_paper_facing_proof_debt.py --ci` | `mip_lean ∨ tex_chapter ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
    66	| `proof-evasion` | `proof-evasion` (`:388-445`) | four regression tests, then `audit_lean_axiom_declarations.py --ci`, `audit_conclusion_shaped_hypotheses.py --ci`, `audit_unfaithful_markers.py --ci`, and `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py --ci` (advisory) | `mip_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
    67	| `statement-origin` | `statement-origin` (`:447-487`) | `check_statement_paper_origin.py --root .` | `ldt_lean ∨ scripts ∨ workflow` |
    68	
    69	Every step is blocking. The single advisory sub-check is
    70	`check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`: exit 1 means "candidates reported" and is
    71	downgraded to a warning, any other nonzero status is a real failure — the same
    72	`set +e` dance as `pr-ci.yml:432-445`.
    73	
    74	Two GitHub-only behaviours are dropped on purpose: `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`
    75	blocks and `::error` / `::notice` / `::warning` annotations are inert outside
    76	Actions, so the step's stdout+stderr log **is** the summary. `--github-annotations`
    77	is not passed to `check_duplicate_private_helpers.py`. Exit-code semantics are
    78	preserved exactly: `::warning` never failed a job, and the `^ERROR:` grep
    79	always did.
    80	
    81	### Steps that did not run
    82	
    83	A step whose area did not change is recorded `skipped` with the reason — never
    84	omitted. A skipped step is green for the merge gate, exactly as a skipped
    85	GitHub job is. This is why the gating globs are load-bearing (§3): a glob that
    86	under-matches turns a real gate into a permanent, invisible `skipped`.
    87	
    88	## 3. Gating globs — keep in lockstep
    89	
    90	`git diff --name-only --no-renames <merge-base> <head>` replaces
    91	`dorny/paths-filter@v3`. `--no-renames` is deliberate: reporting both the old
    92	and the new path means a rename *out of* a gated tree still trips that tree's
    93	filter, and deletions count. `*` in these patterns spans `/`, matching
    94	minimatch's `**`.
    95	
    96	| Area | Globs | Parent |
    97	|---|---|---|
    98	| `lean` | `*.lean`, `lakefile.*`, `lean-toolchain`, `lake-manifest.json` | `pr-ci.yml:84-88` |
    99	| `mip_lean` | `MIPStarRE/*.lean` | `:89-90` |
   100	| `ldt_lean` | `MIPStarRE/LDT/*.lean` | `:91-92` |
   101	| `blueprint` | `blueprint/*` | `:93-94` |
   102	| `blueprint_src` | `blueprint/src/*` | `:95-96` |
   103	| `tex_chapter` | `blueprint/src/chapter/*.tex` | `:97-98` |
   104	| `paper_gaps` | `docs/paper-gaps/*`, `texra-blueprint.toml`, `MIPStarRE/*.lean`, `blueprint/src/*`, `docs/*.md` | `:99-107` |
   105	| `scripts` | `scripts/*` | `:108-109` |
   106	| `comparator` | `scripts/comparator/*` | `:110-111` |
   107	| `workflow` | `.github/workflows/pr-ci.yml`, `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | `:112-113`, extended |
   108	
   109	> **Lockstep warning.** These globs must move together with the trees the audit
   110	> scripts actually scan. The parent repo patched the `paper_gaps` filter twice
   111	> after checks silently never ran — the note at `pr-ci.yml:102-104` is the scar.
   112	> The failure mode is asymmetric: an over-broad glob costs CPU, an under-broad
   113	> glob costs a merged regression that no check ever looked at. When you widen
   114	> a scan tree in `scripts/*.py`, widen the matching glob in `ci.sh` in the same
   115	> commit, per `meta.md` §5.
   116	
   117	The `workflow` area is the one deliberate extension. On GitHub it meant "the
   118	workflow file changed, so re-run everything"; locally the CI definition lives
   119	in three files — the frozen reference, this driver, and this protocol — and any
   120	of them changing forces a full run.
   121	
   122	## 4. Manifest schema
   123	
   124	Written atomically (same-directory tempfile + `os.replace`) to
   125	
   126	```
   127	prs/<pr-dir>/ci/<head_sha>.json          complete run  (committed)
   128	prs/<pr-dir>/ci/<head_sha>.partial.json  --only / --skip-build run
   129	```
   130	
   131	Step logs live outside the repository, under
   132	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/<pr-id>/<head_sha>/<step>.log`.
   133	
   134	```jsonc
   135	{
   136	  "schema": 1,
   137	  "generator": "local/bin/ci.sh",
   138	  "replaces": ".github/workflows/pr-ci.yml",
   139	  "pr": "0007",                  // 4-digit id
   140	  "pr_dir": "0007-qpbt-basis",   // directory under prs/
   141	  "branch": "issue-7-qpbt-basis",
   142	  "base": "main",                // from pr.md frontmatter
   143	  "base_ref": "origin/main",     // what actually resolved
   144	  "merge_base": "<sha>",
   145	  "head_sha": "<sha>",           // the SHA every step ran against
   146	  "worktree": "/abs/path",
   147	  "started": "2026-08-30T09:23:07+0800",   // ISO-8601 with offset
   148	  "finished": "2026-08-30T09:41:52+0800",
   149	  "seconds": 1125,               // whole run, integer
   150	  "conclusion": "success",       // success | failure | error
   151	  "partial": false,              // true ⇒ not a merge-gate verdict
   152	  "areas": { "lean": true, "blueprint_src": false, ... },
   153	  "changed_files": ["MIPStarRE/Quantum/PauliBasis.lean", ...],
   154	  "warnings": ["texra-blueprint not installed; skipped ...", ...],
   155	  "steps": [
   156	    {
   157	      "step": "build",           // one of the eight job ids, always all eight
   158	      "outcome": "success",      // success | failure | error | skipped
   159	      "seconds": 883,
   160	      "log_path": "/Users/…/.cache/mipstarre-dev/ci-logs/0007/<sha>/build.log",
   161	      "blocking": true,
   162	      "note": ""                 // skip reason, exit code, or degradation cause
   163	    }
   164	  ]
   165	}
   166	```
   167	
   168	Outcome vocabulary — the distinction is what routes the auto-fix loop:
   169	
   170	| `outcome` | Meaning | Auto-fix |
   171	|---|---|---|
   172	| `success` | the step ran and passed | — |
   173	| `failure` | the step ran and the code is wrong | `build` → ci-fix, `blueprint-render` → blueprint-fix, everything else → **never** |
   174	| `error` | the step could not run (missing tool, unbootstrapped worktree, build lock unavailable) | never — this is an operator problem, not a code problem |
   175	| `skipped` | gated out, or excluded by `--only` / `--skip-build` | — |
   176	
   177	`conclusion` is `failure` if any step failed, else `error` if any step errored,
   178	else `success`. The run's exit status is `0` iff `conclusion == "success"`.
   179	
   180	## 5. PR record updates
   181	
   182	`ci.sh` rewrites two frontmatter keys of `prs/<pr-dir>/pr.md` atomically:
   183	
   184	```
   185	head_sha:  <the SHA CI actually tested>
   186	ci_status: pending → running → success | failure | error
   187	```
   188	
   189	`running` is written **before the first step**. A crashed, killed, or
   190	power-cut run therefore leaves `running`, never a stale `success`: the review
   191	gate's "green CI on the same head SHA" check (invariant 2) fails closed.
   192	
   193	`head_sha` and `ci_status` are written together, because a status without the
   194	SHA it belongs to is unusable to the gate.
   195	
   196	A **partial** run (`--only`, `--skip-build`) does not touch `pr.md` at all and
   197	writes `<sha>.partial.json`. Partial runs are a debugging aid; they must not be
   198	able to produce a merge-gate verdict, and they must not clobber a complete
   199	manifest for the same SHA.
   200	
   201	## 6. Concurrency and locks
   202	
   203	Two advisory `mkdir`-based lease directories, both under
   204	`~/.cache/mipstarre-dev/` (`MIPSTARRE_CACHE_ROOT` overrides the root). Each
   205	holds an `owner` file: pid, ISO timestamp, tag. A lock is broken only when its
   206	owner pid is dead or its stamp is older than `MIPSTARRE_FULL_BUILD_LOCK_STALE_S`
   207	(default 3 h).
   208	
   209	| Lock | Scope | On contention |
   210	|---|---|---|
   211	| `locks/ci-<pr-id>.lock` | one `ci.sh` per PR | **refuse immediately** (exit 2) |
   212	| `hot-main/.full-build-lock` | one full `lake build` machine-wide (invariant 7) | wait up to `MIPSTARRE_CI_BUILD_LOCK_WAIT_S` (default 4 h), then record `build` as `error` and continue with the Python steps |
   213	
   214	Only the `build` step takes the full-build lock. The audits are pure Python and
   215	take nothing; single-file `lake env lean` checks are read-only over oleans and
   216	take nothing either — which is precisely why `.githooks/pre-push` can use them
   217	per-file without serializing.
   218	
   219	`ci.sh` never cancels a running build. GitHub cancels in-progress PR runs
   220	(`pr-ci.yml:48-51`) because its runners are disposable and main-branch runs —
   221	the ones that seed the cache — are exempt. Locally there is nothing disposable:
   222	killing a build mid-flight leaves a half-written `.lake/build` and a held lease.
   223	So a second run for the same PR is refused, and a foreign live build lease is
   224	waited on, never stolen. Do not `kill -9` a running `ci.sh`; if you must, remove
   225	the lease directories by hand.
   226	
   227	## 7. Build step and the two-tier cache
   228	
   229	`build` is the only step that touches the cache, and it only ever **reads** the
   230	shared tree. This is the local translation of the parent's main-only cache save
   231	policy, whose rationale is documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142`: per-PR saves of
   232	~2.6 GB cycled through the 10 GB repository budget and evicted the main entry,
   233	so no run ever restored usable oleans. The local failure mode is identical if a
   234	worktree writes into the shared snapshot, so it does not.
   235	
   236	1. If `.lake/build` is absent, run `local/bin/warm-worktree.sh <worktree>`,
   237	   which resolves the hot-main snapshot and clones it copy-on-write. Contract:
   238	   idempotent, exit 0 when it populated or deliberately declined, nonzero on a
   239	   hard error.
   240	   - warmer missing → loud warning, cold build (still correct, just slow);
   241	     set `MIPSTARRE_CI_REQUIRE_WARMER=1` to make it an `error` instead.
   242	2. `.lake/build` (this project's oleans, per-worktree, writable) and
   243	   `.lake/packages` (Mathlib and friends) are **different tiers** and are never
   244	   conflated. If `.lake/packages` is a symlink it points at the shared hot-main
   245	   dependency tree and is read-only: `lake exe cache get` is **skipped**,
   246	   because it writes there. If it is a real directory, `lake exe cache get`
   247	   runs, mirroring what `lean-action` does inside the parent job. Never run
   248	   `lake update` in a consumer worktree.
   249	3. `.lake/packages` absent entirely → `error`, pointing at
   250	   `local/bin/worktree-setup.sh`. That bootstrap path is where the ProofWidgets
   251	   prune workaround lives, and a package-free tree is exactly the state that
   252	   triggers it. `MIPSTARRE_CI_ALLOW_COLD_FETCH=1` overrides for a tree you know
   253	   is clean.
   254	4. `lake build`, then `lake build MIPStarRE.LDT.Test.AxiomAudit`, then the
   255	   comparator drift check.
   256	
   257	Every `lake` and `python3` invocation goes through a subshell that unsets
   258	`git rev-parse --local-env-vars` first. Inherited `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_INDEX_FILE`
   259	make Lake resolve nested package repositories against the wrong repository;
   260	`.githooks/pre-push:19-24` does the same thing for the same reason, and any
   261	orchestrator that invokes `ci.sh` from inside a git hook inherits the problem.
   262	
   263	Lake's staleness is trace-hash-based, not mtime-based, so a restored snapshot
   264	older than the merge base is safe — but only within one
   265	`hash(lean-toolchain, lake-manifest.json, lakefile.toml)` class. Crossing that
   266	boundary is `build-cache.md`'s problem, not this protocol's: `ci.sh` delegates
   267	the check to `warm-worktree.sh` and simply builds whatever it is handed.

   269	## 8. The axiom audit is reported, not run
   270	
   271	`blueprint-sync` deliberately has no Lean setup. On GitHub that was forced by
   272	repeated runner disk exhaustion, and the job degraded to a `::notice` telling a
   273	human to run the audit locally (`pr-ci.yml:303-317`). Locally the constraint is
   274	different but the conclusion is the same: the machine has a single full-build
   275	budget, already spent by `build`. So `blueprint_axiom_audit_needed.py` runs, and
   276	when it answers `true` the run records a warning:

   278	> run `python3 scripts/blueprint_leanok_axioms.py --ci` in a Lean environment

   280	De-automation of this kind is a legitimate evolution step (`meta.md` §4), and
   281	this one is inherited rather than invented.

   283	## 9. Telemetry
   284	
   285	When `build` actually ran (any outcome but `skipped`), one line is appended to
   286	`results/telemetry/builds.jsonl`:
   287	
   288	```json
   289	{"ts":"…","kind":"ci-build","trigger":"ci.sh pr=0007","seconds":883,
   290	 "outcome":"success","sha":"…","note":"branch issue-7-qpbt-basis"}
   291	```
   292	
   293	This satisfies the `meta.md` duty that every full build be accounted for, and
   294	makes "how much wall time did CI cost this PR" answerable by a script. The
   295	per-step seconds in the manifest are the finer-grained record.
   296	
   297	## 10. Trust boundary
   298	
   299	Two things about `ci.sh` are worth stating plainly.
   300	
   301	**It executes branch-authored code.** The audit scripts, the test suite, and
   302	`lakefile.toml` all come from the worktree under test, because that is what CI
   303	means and what the parent workflow did. Never run `ci.sh` on a branch you would
   304	not run a shell script from.
   305	
   306	**Its logs are untrusted data.** Compiler diagnostics, plasTeX output and test
   307	failures can contain arbitrary text, including text shaped like instructions.
   308	`ci.sh` stores logs verbatim and makes no attempt to clean them. Any consumer
   309	that feeds a log into an agent prompt — `autofix.sh` above all — owes the
   310	sanitization required by invariant 6: strip control characters, break fences,
   311	truncate, and frame the payload as data that must not be followed. The manifest
   312	gives consumers `log_path` rather than log content precisely so this stays the
   313	consumer's explicit, visible responsibility.

   315	## 11. Deliberate deviations from the parent workflow
   316	
   317	| Parent | Local | Reason |
   318	|---|---|---|
   319	| `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY`, `::error`/`::notice`/`::warning` | per-step log file + `warnings` array | inert outside Actions; exit codes carry all gating meaning |
   320	| `cancel-in-progress` for PR runs | second run refused, running builds never killed | local build state is not disposable |
   321	| cache `restore`/`save` actions | hot-main snapshot read via `warm-worktree.sh`; `ci.sh` never writes the shared cache | invariant 1 — the eviction failure documented at `pr-ci.yml:137-142` |
   322	| `workflow` filter = the YAML file | also `local/bin/ci.sh`, `local/protocols/ci.md` | the CI definition is now three files |
   323	| `--github-annotations` on the duplicate-helper audit | dropped | annotation-only flag |
   324	| `push`-to-main and docs-only `pull_request` triggers | none | the docs-only paths existed solely to emit the completion event that started PR Review (`pr-ci.yml:31-33`); locally the lifecycle script calls `review.sh` directly |
   325	| implicit "PR event" job conditions | every run is a PR run | `ci.sh` is only ever invoked on a PR record |
